context: Tatsuya-country and Hiroshi-elder discuss a historic battle.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 兄ちゃん、昔の合戦、知っとるか?
lines.en: Brother — you know about those old battles?
lines.style: Slow, patient opening. Warm curiosity underneath. Rural Tohoku cadence, unhurried. Settling into shared memory like settling into an old chair.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: おう、歴代の武士、闘ってきた時代や。
lines.en: Yeah — the age when samurai fought through the generations.
lines.style: Gentle affirmation. Kansai lilt on the tail. Thoughtful exhale between clauses. The voice of someone who's held these stories for decades.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 反乱、長年、起こりよった。
lines.en: Rebellions kept rising year after year back then.
lines.style: Soft, matter-of-fact. No drama — just stating what was. Slightly drawn-out syllables. The cadence of someone who lets silence do half the talking.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 深い歴史や、尊重せなあかん。
lines.en: Deep history — something we have to hold with respect.
lines.style: Quiet conviction. Each word placed deliberately. Kansai warmth in the closing particle. Speaking from lived understanding, not recitation.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 我々、平和に感謝、ようけや。
lines.en: We've got so much to be grateful for — all this peace.
lines.style: Solid, grounded tone. Not sentimental but genuinely moved. Slight firmness on gratitude. Tohoku earth in the voice — rooted, real.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お前、ええ視点、持っとるな。
lines.en: You've got a good way of seeing things.
lines.style: Genuine praise, understated. Warm recognition without flattery. Slight lean forward in the voice — elder affirming younger. Brief, because it means more that way.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: おおきに、こうやって、話せて嬉しい。
lines.en: Thank you — I'm grateful we get to talk like this.
lines.style: Soft, sincere close. Unhurried pace. Small smile in the voice without showing teeth. The tenderness of a man not used to saying such things out loud, but meaning every word.
